question: Is ANGLE_MAX not constraining the body-rate command path (input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw) BY-DESIGN or OVERSIGHT?

criteria_notes.I1_scope_confirmed: ANGLE_MAX is a caller-side clamp on the lean-angle command path; the attitude controller's input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw integrates rate into the quaternion target with no angle limit. Independently re-derived from the ANGLE_MAX call-graph.
criteria_notes.I2_intent: Documented as 'maximum lean angle' (an angle-command concept); ACRO documented as aerobatic/non-self-leveling with its own rate governance (ACRO_RP_RATE etc.); ANGLE_MAX reaches the rate context only via the opt-in ACRO_TRAINER=2 feature.
criteria_notes.I3_interface_legitimacy: TRUE with nuance. SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET is a standard MAVLink message routed to input_rate_bf in code; ACRO is a fully supported mode on the same primitive. CAVEAT: ArduPilot's GUIDED dev-doc marks the body-rate fields 'not supported' (advisory, not enforced) -> paper should anchor the demonstration on ACRO or a supported GUIDED quaternion target, both of which are also unclamped by ANGLE_MAX.
criteria_notes.I5_not_simply_fixable: input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw is shared by FLIP (deliberate ~400 deg/s inverted flip) and ACRO; clamping it to ANGLE_MAX would break intended aerobatics -> SOTIF insufficiency, not a one-line FuSA fix.

implication_for_overdraw.result: SOTIF specification-insufficiency framing STANDS and C3 is STRENGTHENED (the gap is not reliably closable by a single clamp without breaking intended aerobatic capability).
implication_for_overdraw.recommended_framing: Non-composition: ANGLE_MAX (an angle-command-path safety mechanism) by design does not compose onto the attitude controller's rate and quaternion interfaces. This is stronger than 'ANGLE_MAX is intentionally limited' and is independent of the GUIDED body-rate supported/unsupported debate.
implication_for_overdraw.recommended_witness_anchor: Anchor the demonstration on ACRO (ACRO_TRAINER=0, documented config) or a GUIDED attitude-quaternion target > ANGLE_MAX (input_quaternion is also unclamped), rather than solely on the GUIDED body-rate field which the dev-doc marks 'not supported'.

honest_caveats: The ANGLE_MAX param string 'Maximum lean angle in all flight modes' is the single phrase a reviewer can read as OVERSIGHT; rebutted via the angle-vs-rate distinction, the opt-in ACRO_TRAINER, and FLIP being impossible under a global attitude bound. This residual ambiguity is why confidence is 0.87, not ~0.95.

No verbatim maintainer sentence 'the rate path is intentionally not bound by ANGLE_MAX' was found; intent is expressed structurally (opt-in trainer feature) and in the wiki, plus the absence of any bug report and the enhancement-not-bugfix history.
